metaDescription: We compared five 30L VEVOR ultrasonic cleaners on wattage, transducers, degas and gentle modes, controls and handles to help you pick the right large tank.
introParagraphs: A 30L ultrasonic cleaner is the size people reach for when a countertop tub is too small, such as for carburetors, a tray of hardware, a set of tools or a handful of watch bands. It holds a lot of liquid, so it can swallow bulky parts, but it also takes real bench space and weighs a lot once filled.

We evaluated five 30L models based on product specs and buyer feedback, all from VEVOR, which dominates this size class. They look alike on a shelf, so the comparison focuses on what actually differs: wattage where listed, transducer count, degas and gentle modes, knob versus digital controls, and how easy each tank is to handle and drain.
Use the picks below to narrow the field, then work through the buying criteria and decision tables to decide which control style and feature set suit the parts you actually clean.

products.name: VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W with Degas and Gentle
products.description:
The VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner is the most complete model in this group, with 600W at 40 kHz, heating from 0 to 80°C, digital controls and a timer. It adds an upgraded degassing mode and a gentle mode, so you can step the power down for delicate pieces or run full strength for greasy parts. The chamber and basket are 304 stainless steel, with a portable handle and a convenient drain.

The listing says degassing boosts working efficiency by 30%, which we treat as a manufacturer claim rather than a measured result. At 600W it is the highest wattage listed among these five, though not every listing publishes a figure. The tradeoff is the usual large-tank one, since a full 30L of water is heavy and needs a sturdy bench and a plan for draining.

In daily use you fill with warm water and a neutral detergent, run degas for a few minutes, wash and drain. Compared with the VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner 480W with Digital Display it adds 120W, degas and a gentle mode. Next to the VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control, which uses dials, it is the fully digital version of the same idea.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants one 30L tank for tools, parts and the occasional delicate item.
pros: The 600W output at 40 kHz is the highest wattage listed in this group
A gentle mode steps power down for fragile items and precision work
Degas mode clears dissolved gas before the real cleaning cycle
Heating from 0 to 80°C helps dissolve grease, oil and wax residue
cons: A full 30L tank is heavy, so it needs a sturdy bench and drain plan
The degassing efficiency figure is a maker claim, not a tested result
More tank and power than a few rings or a retainer would ever need

products.name: VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with 10 Transducers and Heater
products.description:
This VEVOR 30L uses ten sandwich-type piezoelectric transducers at 40 kHz, which is the highest transducer count in the group. A digital control panel sets time and temperature, a heating function is built in, and the listing mentions multiple modes for different items. The tank and basket are SUS304 stainless steel, and the listing positions it for jewelry, eyeglasses, watches, laboratories and carburetors.

The listing gives no total wattage, so the transducer count is the best sign of output but not a direct comparison with the 600W model. More transducers tend to spread energy across a larger tank floor, which can help with even cleaning of a full basket. The tradeoff is that mode names and heater range are not spelled out, so check the manual for details.

Ownership follows the same fill, warm, run and drain routine as the others. Compared with the VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W with Degas and Gentle it lacks a named gentle mode, and next to the VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner 480W with Digital Display it brings a bigger transducer array and an explicit heater. The listing mentions certifications without naming them, so look for markings on the unit.
products.bestFor: Users who want broad cleaning coverage across a full basket of mixed small items.
pros: Ten sandwich transducers give the largest array of any pick here
A digital panel sets time and temperature without fiddly guesswork
SUS304 stainless steel tank and basket resist corrosion over the years
A built-in heating function helps loosen grease on metal parts
cons: No total wattage is listed, so output cannot be compared directly
Mode names and the heater range are not spelled out in the listing
The certifications are mentioned but not named, so check the unit label

products.name: VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner 480W with Digital Display
products.description:
This VEVOR 30L has 480W of ultrasonic power at 40 kHz and adjustable heating from 0 to 80°C. A digital display shows the settings, and the listing highlights an upgraded handle for moving the tank when it is full. The basket and inner tank are corrosion-resistant stainless steel, and the basket is designed to avoid scratching the items.

It targets jewelry, watches, electronic components and industrial parts with heavy oil stains. At 480W it has the lowest listed output in the group, and it lists no degas or gentle mode, so you control delicacy only through time and temperature. That is fine for sturdy parts, but less forgiving for fragile ones.

The routine is fill, warm, run and drain, with the handle making transport easier, although carrying a full tank is still best avoided. Compared with the VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W with Degas and Gentle it gives up 120W and the two extra modes. Against the VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control it uses a digital display instead of dials.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a straightforward digital 30L for sturdy parts and general cleaning.
pros: A digital display makes time and temperature easy to read at a glance
The 480W output at 40 kHz is enough for general parts and hardware
Heating from 0 to 80°C helps with oil, wax and stubborn grime
An upgraded handle is designed to make full-tank transport easier
cons: At 480W it has the lowest listed output among the five tanks
No degas or gentle mode is listed to protect fragile or finished items
A full 30L tank is still heavy to move, even with the upgraded handle

products.name: VEVOR 30L-Class 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner with Side Handles
products.description:
This VEVOR is sold as a 30L-class cleaner, with 40 kHz cavitation, a digital panel for time and temperature, and adjustable heating from 0 to 80°C. The SUS304 stainless tank comes with a cleaning basket that keeps items away from the tank wall, and side handles make it easier to move. The listing names carburetor components, nozzles, watchbands, small hardware, lab tools and workstation parts.

The 30L-class wording is worth noting, because it suggests approximately rather than exactly 30L, so confirm the working volume before relying on it. No wattage is listed, so as with the ten-transducer model you cannot directly compare power. It is a practical, no-frills option with fewer headline features than the degas and gentle model.

Expect the usual fill, warm, run and drain routine, with the side handles making placement easier when the tank is empty. Compared with the VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W with Degas and Gentle it has no named special modes, and next to the VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control it uses a digital readout instead of dials.
products.bestFor: People who want handles on the sides and a digital panel for parts and hardware.
pros: Side handles make positioning and storing the empty unit easier
A digital panel shows time and temperature for repeatable cycles
The basket keeps items off the tank wall to reduce scratching
The SUS304 tank resists corrosion, with heating from 0 to 80°C
cons: The 30L-class label suggests an approximate volume, so verify capacity
No wattage or named special modes are listed in the product details
Fewer headline features than the degas and gentle 600W model

products.name: VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control
products.description:
The VEVOR 30L Knob Control model runs at 40 kHz and lets you set frequency, time and temperature with a simple knob, backed by a digital display. It includes a degassing mode that the listing says boosts efficiency by 30%, plus two power settings for delicate or heavy-duty work. The tank is 304 stainless steel, and the package adds a basket and a cleaning ball.

The dial layout is the draw if small touch buttons are awkward, since a turn is easier to feel than a tap on a flat panel. No wattage is listed, so you cannot weigh its output against the 600W or 480W models. It is aimed at carburetors, spray nozzles and small parts, and the listing asks for a neutral detergent and warm water.

Ownership is fill, add detergent, degas, run, drain and dry the basket. It offers a similar degas and power-step approach to the VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W with Degas and Gentle, just with dials rather than digital buttons. Compared with the VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner 480W with Digital Display it adds degassing and a second power setting.
products.bestFor: People who find dials easier than buttons and want degas on a 30L tank.
pros: Knobs set frequency, time and temperature with simple, tactile turns
Degassing and dual power settings cover delicate and heavy-duty work
A stainless basket and a cleaning ball are included in the package box
The 40 kHz output reaches carburetor channels, nozzles and small holes
cons: No wattage is listed, so output cannot be compared with other tanks
Dial settings are harder to repeat exactly than numbers on a display
Another heavy 30L tank that needs a stable bench and a drain plan

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 30L label is only a starting point, because usable space depends on the basket and the fill line. Items should sit in the basket, clear of the walls, with liquid covering them fully. Four of these machines are sold simply as 30L, but the VEVOR 30L-Class 40kHz Ultrasonic Cleaner uses a class label, so confirm the working volume in the manual. A 30L tank holds roughly 30 kg of water, so also plan the bench, the drain route and a spot to store it.

Ultrasonic watts and transducer count together hint at cleaning power. A larger array spreads energy, and more watts clean faster, but pieces can suffer if power is too high. The VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W lists 600W, the VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner 480W lists 480W, and the ten-transducer model lists no wattage at all. Compare wattage per liter when it is given, which is 20W per liter for 600W and 16W per liter for 480W, and ask when a listing leaves it out.

Controls decide how pleasant the machine is to use week after week. Dials are easy to grip and read from a distance, while digital panels allow exact, repeatable settings. The VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control uses knobs plus a digital display, while the 600W model, the 480W model, the ten-transducer model and the 30L-Class model use digital panels. If you wear gloves or have stiff fingers, dials are the easier choice.

Fresh water holds dissolved gas that damps cavitation, so a degas run of a few minutes before the real wash makes the first load work better. A gentle mode lowers power for fragile or finished items. The VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W lists both, the Knob Control model lists degas and dual power, and the 480W, ten-transducer and 30L-Class models list neither by name. If your parts vary from rough to finished, favor a model that can step power down.

A full 30L tank is too heavy to carry, so handles are for moving the empty unit and the real question is how you drain it. The VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W lists a portable handle and a convenient drain, the 480W model lists an upgraded handle, and the 30L-Class model has side handles. Choose a spot near a sink or bucket, drain the tank before you lift it, and never carry it while it still holds liquid. A bench next to the drain beats lifting a full tank every time.

Heat to about 50 to 60°C helps with grease and wax, and all five machines here list heating, with most reaching 0 to 80°C. A neutral detergent works best with warm water, as the VEVOR Knob Control listing advises. Always use the basket, since parts resting on the tank floor can scratch it and clean unevenly. Keep rubber, glued parts and soft plastics out of long, hot cycles.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and transducer design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared listed wattage, frequency and transducer count across the five tanks. The VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner leads on listed output at 600W, the 480W model follows, and the ten-transducer model leads on array size. We treated all figures as manufacturer claims and weighed them against what buyer feedback describes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Modes and delicate-item care
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which tanks list degas, gentle and dual power settings, since a 30L machine is often shared between tools and finished parts. The 600W model lists degas and gentle, the Knob Control model lists degas and dual power, and the other three list neither. That gap carried real weight in our rankings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and readability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared knobs against digital displays, timer and temperature control, and how clearly each listing describes the interface. The Knob Control model pairs dials with a display, while the other four are digital. We rated simplicity and repeatability, with extra credit where the interface is easy for stiff or gloved hands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at handles, drains, basket inclusion and weight, since those decide how annoying a 30L tank is week to week. The 600W model lists a handle and drain, the 480W model an upgraded handle, and the 30L-Class model side handles. The Knob Control model adds a cleaning ball and basket.

howWeEvaluated.title: Materials and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered stainless grades, tank and basket build, and what each model includes. The 600W, ten-transducer and 30L-Class models name 304 or SUS304 stainless, and the 480W lists corrosion-resistant stainless. We did not rank on price figures, only on what each model offers for its class within this lineup.

cards.label: Knob dials
cards.text: A dial lets you turn to a setting by feel, which suits gloves and stiff fingers, and there are fewer menus to forget. The trade is less exact repeatability. The VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control sits on this side, with a digital display to confirm settings. Pick dials for quick, simple operation.

The VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W with Degas and Gentle, the 10 Transducers and Heater model, the 480W model and the 30L-Class model all use panels. Pick a panel for repeatable settings.

faq.q: Which 30L ultrasonic cleaner is best overall?
faq.a: The VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W with Degas and Gentle is the best all-rounder here, with 600W at 40 kHz, heating to 80°C, and both degas and gentle modes. If you prefer dials, the Knob Control model adds degas and dual power. For basic general cleaning, the 480W digital model is a simpler choice with lower listed output.

faq.q: How much counter space and weight should I plan for?
faq.a: A 30L tank holds roughly 30 kg of water, plus the weight of the machine, so you need a sturdy bench or workshop table. Plan a spot near a sink or bucket so you can drain before moving. Handles on these models are for moving the empty unit, not a full one.

faq.q: Does more wattage always mean better cleaning?
faq.a: Not always. More ultrasonic watts clean faster but can stress delicate or finished parts, and the tank design and transducer layout matter too. The VEVOR 600W model and the 480W model differ by 120W, while the ten-transducer model gives no wattage at all. Look for gentle or adjustable power if you clean mixed items.

faq.q: Do I need a degas mode?
faq.a: It helps. Fresh tap water holds dissolved gas that cushions cavitation bubbles, so the first minutes of a cycle are weaker. A degas run clears that gas before the real wash. The 600W model and the Knob Control model list degassing, and the listings claim a 30% efficiency gain, which is a maker figure.

faq.q: Is it safe to clean jewelry in a 30L industrial-style tank?
faq.a: Only with care. A 40 kHz tank is more aggressive than a small jewelry tub, and soft or porous stones such as pearls, opals, turquoise and emeralds can crack or cloud. Treated, loose or antique prong pieces can also be shaken loose. Use a gentle mode, such as on the VEVOR 30L Sonic Cleaner 600W, and keep cycles short.

The VEVOR Knob Control listing advises a neutral detergent with warm water, which is a sound default for general parts. Avoid strong acids or solvents unless the manual allows them, since they can damage the tank and baskets or create hazards when heated. Always rinse and dry parts after cleaning.

faq.q: How should I maintain a 30L ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: Drain it after each session, wipe out any sludge and dry the tank and basket to prevent spots. Never run it without liquid, and do not leave the heater on an empty tank. Replace the solution when it turns cloudy or oily, and keep the control area dry. Use the basket every time.
